content.title: About
content.content: Chickpeas are a legume whose seeds are widely used in cuisines around the world. Dried chickpeas with no added fat are fully dehydrated beans ready for further cooking. They have a nutty flavor, firm texture, and a rich nutrient profile.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chickpeas are one of the oldest cultivated crops, grown in ancient Egypt and Mesopotamia.
Dried chickpeas can be stored for up to a year when kept in proper conditions, retaining their nutritional value.
In India chickpeas are called “chana” and feature in dishes such as chana masala, chaat, and hummus.
Chickpeas are high in protein, making them a popular meat alternative in vegetarian and vegan diets.
There are several varieties – Kabuli, Desi, small, large – each with distinct culinary uses.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: Chickpeas contain about 20 % protein by weight, providing essential amino acids for those who avoid animal products.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestive health, promotes satiety, and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Complex carbs deliver steady energy without causing rapid glucose spikes.

items.title: Contains iron and folate
items.content: These micronutrients are important for blood formation and preventing anemia, especially in women of childbearing age.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The absence of added fat makes dried chickpeas suitable for low‑fat dietary plans.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chickpeas, ranging from skin rashes to severe anaphylaxis.

items.title: Phytic acid
items.content: Chickpeas contain phytates that can reduce mineral absorption; soaking and sprouting lower their levels.

items.title: Gas and bloating
items.content: Legumes can cause gastrointestinal discomfort in sensitive people; gradual introduction helps the gut adapt.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Dried chickpeas should be soaked in water for at least 8–12 hours, then boiled until tender. They are used in soups, stews, salads, grain bowls, and for making hummus or vegetarian patties.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dry chickpeas in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For extended storage, keep them in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent mold and flavor loss.
